brief:
Palestinian citizens of Israel, who comprise roughly 16% of eligible voters in Tuesday's election, report that major candidates are sidelining their concerns while pledging ethnic cleansing, according to Zeteo. Diana Buttu, a Palestinian analyst, wrote that despite their significant electoral share, Palestinian citizens face a political landscape where their issues receive minimal attention from mainstream parties.

Buttu contended that across the Israeli political spectrum, candidates converge on a shared objective of displacing the Palestinian population, leaving Palestinian voters without meaningful representation of their interests or protection of their rights in the electoral process.
dek: Palestinians make up around 16% of the eligible voters in Tuesday’s election – yet our issues are ignored and candidates promise the same goal: to ethnically cleanse us, writes Diana Buttu.
title: Palestinian citizens say Israeli election ignores their needs, promises displacement
